source.title: Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization

exact_header:
theorem stronglyConvex_existsUnique_minimizer {E : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (d : ℕ) (e : E ≃ₗ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (f : E → EReal) (lam : ℝ)
    (hf : SourceProper f) (hclosed : SourceClosed f)
    (hlam : 0 < lam)
    (hstrong : ∀ x ∈ effectiveDomain f, ∀ y ∈ effectiveDomain f,
      ∀ a : ℝ, 0 < a → a < 1 →
      f (a • x + (1 - a) • y) ≤
        (a : EReal) * f x + ((1 - a : ℝ) : EReal) * f y -
          (((lam / 2) * a * (1 - a) * ‖x - y‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : EReal))
    (hsub : {p : E |
      (SourceSubdifferential (fun u => f (e.symm u)) (e p)).Nonempty}.Nonempty) :
    ∃! p : E, p ∈ effectiveDomain f ∧ ∀ q : E, f p ≤ f q
source_proof_topology: Choose source support y,g; quadratic-affine lower bound plus dual-norm/reverse-triangle inequality gives f(x)→+∞ as normx→∞; bounded closed sublevels compact; A.3 supplies minimum; strict convexity yields uniqueness.
implementation_topology: Derive convex effective domain and coordinate properness internally. Supplied hsub yields y,g and actual finite y.
Form continuous L(v)=inner(g,e(v)) in original norm. For S={x|f(x)≤f(y)}, source-vector growth and operator norm give (λ/2)||x−y||²≤||L||||x−y||, hence S⊆closedBall(y,2||L||/λ).
SourceClosed gives S closed; finite dimensionality from e gives compact closed ball. Therefore S compact.
SourceClosed↔LSC and y∈S∩effectiveDomain feed actual A.3. Its returned minimum is finite because S⊆effectiveDomain and SourceProper excludes bottom.
For q outsideS, f(y)<f(q), hence p minimizes globally. Actual Minimum growth atp and λ>0 force any other minimizer to coincide.
proof_route_delta: Direct compactness of one nonempty sublevel replaces explicit global coercivity-limit derivation. It proves exactly the compactness needed by A.3 from source premises; does not add compactness/coercivity assumptions. Uniqueness uses quantitative Minimum growth rather than a separate strict-convexity theorem. Preserve source and implementation graphs distinctly.
